pages.text: One sunny afternoon, <name> wandered through the village market and spotted a dusty old lantern in a quiet corner. When he touched it, it glowed softly. A tiny voice purred, “I grant wishes—but only kind ones.”
A sleek talking cat with bright green eyes appeared. “Follow me,” it said. “The lantern will shine for good deeds, but beware—a greedy merchant wants it for himself.”

<name> nodded and looked around the village. The streets were dark and quiet. People whispered about broken lamps, empty shelves, and shadows in every corner. He wished quietly: “I hope we can bring light and happiness back to everyone.” The lantern shimmered and sparkled, lighting the village square.

Just then, the greedy merchant appeared, snatching the lantern. “It should belong to me!” he demanded. But the lantern glowed brighter, sending a warm golden light that made the merchant stumble backward. <name> realized that the lantern’s magic worked strongest when helping others.

With the talking cat’s clues, <name> went from house to house. He wished for small joys: a lost kitten returned to its owner, a baker’s oven filled with fresh bread, and a little girl’s lamp shining bright for bedtime stories. Each kind wish made the lantern sparkle even more, and soon the whole village glowed warmly.
Seeing the happiness around him, the merchant softened. He apologized and helped <name> spread the lantern’s light, learning that giving was more magical than taking.

<name> placed the lantern in the village square, where it glimmered day and night. People laughed, shared stories, and felt warmth in every corner. The talking cat purred and curled up beside him, and <name> smiled, knowing that kindness could shine brighter than anything else in the world.
